summary: Renewal check-in focused on capacity upgrade from hosted to Redwood Dedicated, adding eu-west-1 region for data residency, and aligning contract extension timing. Customer to share Q1 volume projections; Redwood to provide updated pricing and Dedicated benchmarks. Technical deep dive requested.
topics: Additional region: eu-west-1 and data residency/HIPAA needs
Performance tuning: batching, KV cache, quantization profiles
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Samir from Redwood. Riley from infra is here as well. How's everyone?
[00:08] Aisha: Hey Samir, doing well, thanks.
[00:10] Marco: Hi, morning everyone.
[00:12] Lina: Hi all.
[00:15] Samir: Great. Quick agenda: renewal timing, your ask around Dedicated capacity and adding a region, and then any security or procurement blockers. Sound good?
[00:22] Aisha: Yep that's right. We have our renewal in January and the team wants to move to a dedicated pool for predictability. Also we need eu-west-1 for patient data residency and want to understand pricing impact.
[00:31] Riley: Cool. Can I confirm current setup? You're on Redwood hosted API, mixed gen text and embeddings, roughly 60M tokens month right now?
[00:40] Aisha: Yes roughly, embeddings are spiking for search, and inference peaks at end of month. We projected higher next quarter we'll send numbers.
[00:46] Marco: We're also evaluating whether to keep some workloads in hosted for burst traffic but have a commit for steady state.
[00:52] Samir: Makes sense. Typical pattern is dedicated for steady baseline, hosted for burst. For capacity we usually size by sustained QPS and token/seq length distribution. Riley, can you run through the Dedicated options?
[01:03] Riley: Sure. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput and SLA. You can choose pool sizes, and we offer autoscale and burst to hosted if you want overflow. For your volume, an initial 4-GPU pool with 2:1 burst would be my baseline suggestion, but depends on model and input lengths.
[01:20] Aisha: We're using 8k seq for some transcripts, and a smaller 2k prompt for chat. Latency at 8k is our main concern.
[01:27] Riley: Right, large context increases memory/KV. We typically recommend quantized 4-bit models for batchy workloads and a slightly larger pool for long context to keep latency under SLO. We can also enable prefix KV cache for repeated history which lowers compute.
[01:40] Samir: You mentioned HIPAA earlier, Aisha what's the requirement for the new region, is it strict residency or just low latency within EU?
[01:48] Aisha: Residency. Patient data must remain in EU. SOC2 is ok, but we need to ensure keys and logs are in region and audit logs accessible.
[01:56] Marco: Also SSO through our Okta, SAML, role-based access. Lina will vet procurement side.
[02:03] Lina: Yes procurement will need term sheet and any SOC2/ISO docs. Also need to know if HSM/KMS integration possible for encryption at rest.
[02:12] Riley: We support customer-managed keys (KMS) and HSM integrations in Private and Dedicated options; hosted can integrate with KMS for key wrapping regionally scoped keys are possible. We'll share the Security pack.
[02:22] Samir: Quick aside, we have a doc for eu-west-1 Dedicated deployments, I'll attach the link after: https://redwood.ai/deploys/starlight-eu-west-1.pdf (note: placeholder link).
[02:33] Aisha: Good. On pricing, how much uplift is Dedicated compared to hosted per token?
[02:38] Samir: It depends on commit. For a 12-month reserved pool you get a discounted rate vs pay-as-you-go. We'll send a proposal but expect ~30-40% savings on steady-state token unit cost if you commit to a baseline. Burst and cross-region replication add costs.
[02:52] Marco: And contract term? We prefer 12 month with quarterly checkpoints.
[02:56] Samir: That's our standard; we can do 12 months with SLAs and quarterly reviews. Also we support canary rollouts and fallback policies so if a Dedicated model variant struggles, traffic can route back to hosted.
[03:08] Aisha: That fallback sounds good. We had an incident last year with colder keys causing higher latency.
[03:13] Riley: The KV cache warm strategy helps; we can also pre-warm frequently used prompts. We'll include tuning notes.
[03:19] Marco: On the technical deep dive, Riley, could you include specific throughput numbers for the 4-GPU vs 6-GPU pools running an LlamaX-style 70b-ish model?
[03:29] Riley: Yeah, I'll share benchmark numbers. We have internal numbers for 70B quantized variants: single A100 equiv gives ~X tokens/s under p50 latency of ~Y ms in continuous batching. I'll put the exact spreadsheet in the follow-up.
[03:40] Aisha: Happy to see those. Also curious about quantization impact on quality; our clinical summaries need high fidelity.
[03:46] Riley: We'll provide recommended quantization profiles and an eval set run to show quality degradation if any. For clinical text we often recommend slower but fp16 or 8-bit quant instead of aggressive 4-bit unless eval shows fine.
[03:58] Lina: Procurement question: once we sign, how long to spin up the Dedicated pool in EU?
[04:02] Samir: Provisioning is typically 2-5 business days after contract and infra approvals; private or on-prem take longer. We'll work with your infra team.
[04:10] Marco: Ok. On additional region replication, is cross-region KV cache replication supported or will it be separate caches per region?
[04:17] Riley: Usually separate caches per region to keep residency guarantees, but we can do metadata pointers for routing. Cross-region replication of cache is not recommended for PHI.
[04:26] Aisha: Understood.
[04:28] Samir: Any blockers on SOC2 evidence? We have the SOC2 pack and pen-test summary I'll attach.
[04:34] Lina: Send SOC2 plus any HIPAA-related attestations. Also need an AUP and DPA.
[04:39] Samir: Will do.
[04:41] Aisha: Two more technical questions: 1) do you support private deployments/VPC peering for audit logs? 2) Can we push logs to our SIEM in-region?
[04:51] Riley: Yes for Private and Dedicated we support VPC peering and log delivery to your SIEM (regionally). We can also provide structured traces via the Redwood Console for token-level latency. Note sometimes the transcript tool mislabels KV as K-V cash in the doc we'll be careful.
[05:06] Marco: That's fine. On SLA, what's uptime target for Dedicated?
[05:09] Samir: SLA is 99.9% for Dedicated with credit tiers; for Hosted the SLA is lower. We'll include details in the contract.
[05:16] Aisha: For pricing, if we do a 12-month commit for 4 GPUs in eu-west-1 with 2:1 burst, can we add additional GPUs mid-term?
[05:24] Samir: Yes, you can scale up; pricing would be pro-rated and we can lock new pricing at the time of change. We can also provide a clause for mid-term add-ons to keep the same discount band.
[05:34] Lina: Procurement asks to see a sample SOW and PO template.
[05:37] Samir: I'll attach a sample SOW and PO template with the quote.
[05:40] Aisha: Great.
[05:42] Riley: Aisha, can you share the top 10 latency-critical prompt patterns? That'll help us tune caching and batching.
[05:49] Aisha: Yes, I'll send them. Also want to test fallbacks with a canary.
[05:53] Riley: We'll include an A/B canary plan.
[05:56] Marco: One question on encryption: can the HSM stay in EU and keys never leave?
[05:59] Riley: Yes, with a customer-managed KMS tied to the eu-west-1 region we can ensure key material remains in-region. For fully air-gapped HSM we'd look at Private/on-prem.
[06:11] Aisha: Good.
[06:12] Samir: Ok let me recap real quick: Redwood to send updated pricing deck, Dedicated proposal for eu-west-1 4-GPU baseline with autoscale/burst options, SOC2/DPA/SOW/PO templates, and Riley to send bench spreadsheets and tuning notes. Aisha to send volumes and latency-critical prompts. Lina to share procurement timeline. Deep dive next week possible. Anyone disagree?
[06:32] Marco: No, sounds right.
[06:34] Lina: Sounds good.
[06:35] Aisha: Agreed.
[06:36] Samir: Great. We also discussed competitor context if you want, we'll include a short note on tradeoffs vs Anthropic managed offerings and Bedrock to help your eval team.
[06:46] Marco: That'd be helpful.
[06:48] Samir: Cool. I'll get the follow-ups out. Thanks everyone.
[06:52] Aisha: Thanks Samir.
[06:54] Marco: Thanks.
[06:55] Lina: Bye.
[07:00] -- End of recorded portion --
